post.caption: Two Nobel medals once hid in acid. Germany had just occupied Denmark in April 1940. Chemist Georg de Hevesy worked at Niels Bohr's institute in Copenhagen, and he dissolved two German laureates' medals in strong acid. The flask sat on a shelf and the Nazis never noticed. After the war the gold was recovered and new medals were made. Franck's new medal was presented in Chicago in 1952. Today the medals are 18 karat gold with a 24 karat gold coat. Most are 66 millimeters across and weigh about 175 grams. Erik Lindberg designed four of the medals. The Peace medal was designed by sculptor Gustav Vigeland.
